newsitem.title: GERMANY: German November producer, import prices flat.
newsitem.headline: German November producer, import prices flat.

text.p: German producer and import prices data for November released on Friday showed no change against the previous month, reinforcing comments by a central banker that long-term prospects for price stability were excellent.

Pan-German producer prices were flat in November after a 0.2 percent rise in October, while the year-on-year figure was down 0.3 percent, in line with the previous month, the Federal Statistics Office in Wiesbaden said.
A 0.1 percent month-on-month drop in western Germany was offset by a gain of 0.1 percent in the former-communist east.
Meanwhile, separate data showed that import prices were unchanged in November after a 0.6 percent upward blip in October linked to a rally in oil prices. The yearly increase was 1.4 percent.
Before the release of the data, Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing said Germany's chances of maintaining price stability were unprecedented.
"We are in a phase of stability in the value of money, which is favourable as never before," Issing told German television.
November's producer price data showed a sharp 1.4 percent increase in tobacco products, while oil fell back by 1.1 percent.
Import prices -- excluding oil -- rose by 0.2 percent, showing that oil imports had exerted a negative influence on the overall figure.
